rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger. I have no answer for you.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. I have no need of idle offers.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. I have no comment on the captain.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: State your reason for entering, stranger. I have no advice to give without it.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. Trust is earned by evidence, not demanded.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Well now. New, are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Well now, offering help before I’ve even asked. That’s a new one.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Well now. Strict, fair, and not a man you want catching you shirking. Why do you ask?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Well now, asking a gate guard for advice. I’d be guessing, and the captain hates a guess dressed up as fact.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Well now, it is. Makes a patrol almost pleasant, doesn't it?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Well now, you needn’t. I’m asking a question, not asking for your trust.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: You there. Stop. New here, are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? No. Keep moving, and don't make me ask twice.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? What’s that to you?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Into the city? Ask someone who knows. I’ve nothing for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You shouldn't. Keep your distance and answer straight.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, love, new to the yard, are you? It's the inn, though you can see I'm keeping busy with the work out here.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, love, that's kind of you to ask. I'm keeping the yard in hand just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, I make of him what I make of most folk—best to see how he treats people before deciding.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, love, I’m busy keeping this yard in hand, and I’ve no advice for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: It is, love. Makes this yard a pleasure to tend.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh, love, you needn't trust me. I’ve only got the yard to mind and supper to see to.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. I don't know what you mean by “this place.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: What? Keep your hands clear of the stock. If you know smithing, put them to the work; otherwise, don't get in my way.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: What about him? I've work to finish.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: What. I’m working; I’ve no advice for getting into the city.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. Weather won't finish this work.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You don't have to. Now, what is it?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh! You're new? I'm Jory, and I'm meant to be helping at the forge, but I can't tell you much about the place, I'm afraid—Aunt Mara keeps me busy.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh! You want to help? I’m just seeing to the forge, but Aunt Mara says I ought to keep at it, and I’m keeping at it.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh! The captain? I don't know them, so I can't say—and now I'm wondering what they're like.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh! The city, you say? I don't know anything useful about getting in, but how far have you come to reach it?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh! Is it? I’ve been at the forge and hardly looked up, but now you’ve said it I’ll have to see for myself!

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh! You don’t have to, I suppose—but I’m only helping at the forge, and I’m not asking you for anything. What made you wonder?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Keep clear of the timber. I’m in the middle of work.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Mind the timber. If you've a hand to spare, keep clear of the tools while I work.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I’ve no measure of the captain to give you.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Keep clear of the timber, then. I’ve nothing useful to tell you about the city.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Mind the timber. Aye, it is.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Mind the timber. Trust is earned by sound work, not words.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Friend! New to the town, are you? That question's worth a little trade—what are you looking to learn?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Friend, a hand is worth what it earns. What would you put on the table for mine?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Friend, a captain's worth is measured by what he can secure—and what it costs to deal with him. What value do you put on yours?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Friend, advice is a bargain like any other. What would you put on the table for it?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Friend, fine enough for trade, I’d say. What’s the weather worth to you?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Friend, trust is a risk like any other. What would make the bargain worth it to you?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Stranger. New here, by your account. I’m watching the south road.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: You’re standing on the south road. I have the watch.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: You asked what I make of him. I’ve nothing to report.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Stranger. You need the city. I have no advice for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear sky. I can see the south road to its end.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. I report what I see.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Hm. Ask someone else.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Hm. No.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Hm. What’s there to make?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Hm. Ask someone else.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Hm. Weather.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Hm. You shouldn't.
